{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOLEgSIs8AAAABXcWt5w", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bm7fazhBAjKc", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bm7fa", "number": 11, "title": "Modernize WebXR APIs and spec conformance for Quest 3 and Android AR emulation", "body": "## Problem

After Issues #3, #5, #7 and #9, the extension has strict TypeScript, Manifest V3, modern Three.js, and exactly two emulator profiles. However, the WebXR API surface and parts of its behavior are still based on an old `webxr-polyfill` architecture. The README explicitly references the **10 October 2019** WebXR Device API draft. Applications using current WebXR APIs can observe missing interfaces, incorrect feature negotiation, and inaccurate error, input, hit-test or frame semantics.

This is the next **WebXR standards and API compatibility** effort, not another device-profile, bundler, Three.js or manifest migration. Do not confuse successful rendering in the existing smoke fixture with actual WebXR specification conformance.

## Expected outcome

Modernize the emulator's observable WebXR APIs to the **latest published W3C WebXR Device API (9 June 2026 Candidate Recommendation Draft as of this Issue)** and the applicable published modules/editor drafts available at implementation time. Fix existing spec mismatches and provide useful, deterministic simulated implementations of contemporary APIs for **Meta Quest 3 (VR/MR)** and **Generic Android Phone (ARCore)**, with a documented, tested feature/capability matrix.

For each API/module: either (a) implement the API with semantically correct behavior on the supported virtual device(s), or (b) accurately report it as unsupported, with explicit rationale and correct required/optional feature negotiation. **Never claim a feature is supported solely because a stub exists.** For modules explicitly marked below as implementation targets, do not close the Issue by only documenting them as unsupported; record intentionally missing scope and leave this Issue open or follow the repository's partial-PR process.

Hardware fidelity, real environment sensing, permission bypasses, and unsupported browser/OS APIs are not required. Deterministic simulated spatial data is appropriate, but returned poses, spaces, textures and events must be internally coherent and follow the API contracts.

## Context

- Follow [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/development-flow.md), [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/blob/dev/docs/review-guidelines.md), and the Issue/PR templates. Use English for Issues, PRs and commits; start from and target `dev`.
- Device consolidation [Issue #9](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/issues/9) / [PR #10](https://github.com/takahirox/WebXR-emulator-extension/pull/10) is merged: only `Meta Quest 3` (VR/MR toggle, two tracked controllers) and `Generic Android Phone (ARCore)` (monoscopic handheld AR/touch) are selectable. Keep that selection, mode switching, persistence, and existing WebXR features intact.
- Key code: `src/polyfill/CustomWebXRPolyfill.ts`, `src/polyfill/EmulatedXRDevice.ts`, `src/polyfill/api/`, `src/polyfill/ARScene.ts`, `src/types/`, `src/devices.json`, `src/app/panel.ts`, and `tests/`. `webxr-polyfill` is referenced via internal, private imports; assess whether upgrading, patching/forking, or replacing the dependency is required for current spec semantics. Avoid fragile prototype monkey-patches if a maintainable API-based alternative exists.
- Confirmed concrete gaps in the current source:
  - `CustomWebXRPolyfill.ts` creates hit-test sources without checking the session's enabled `hit-test` feature, ended session state, or frame/source validity; DOM Overlay currently only handles `optionalFeatures`, not `requiredFeatures` and missing root semantics.
  - `XRHitTestSource.ts` and transient counterpart reject nonempty `entityTypes`, have incomplete `cancel()` semantics, and require lifecycle/error validation; `EmulatedXRDevice.ts` currently drops the hit surface orientation in generated poses.
  - Core session and frame behavior still depends on old `webxr-polyfill` internals; inspect `XRSession.enabledFeatures`, visibility, events, reference-space support, input source ordering, view/pose validity, XR frame lifetime, WebGL binding and resource lifecycle against the modern specification.
  - The emulator should not advertise support for extensions it does not implement or for features invalid for the current profile/mode.
- Baseline official references (reconfirm exact versions and status when implementing):
  - [WebXR Device API, 9 June 2026 CRD](https://www.w3.org/TR/webxr/)
  - [WebXR AR Module](https://www.w3.org/TR/webxr-ar-module-1/)
  - [WebXR Hit Test Module, 11 December 2025 WD](https://www.w3.org/TR/webxr-hit-test-1/)
  - [WebXR DOM Overlays Module](https://www.w3.org/TR/webxr-dom-overlays-1/)
  - [WebXR Gamepads Module](https://www.w3.org/TR/webxr-gamepads-module-1/)
  - [WebXR Hand Input Module](https://www.w3.org/TR/webxr-hand-input-1/)
  - [WebXR Layers API Level 1, 11 August 2026 WD](https://www.w3.org/TR/webxrlayers-1/)
  - [WebXR Anchors editor's draft](https://immersive-web.github.io/anchors/)
  - [WebXR Depth Sensing Module, 25 August 2026 WD](https://www.w3.org/TR/webxr-depth-sensing-1/)
  - [WebXR Lighting Estimation editor's draft](https://immersive-web.github.io/lighting-estimation/)
  - [Web Platform Tests, WebXR](https://wpt.fyi/results/webxr) and [WebXR Samples](https://immersive-web.github.io/webxr-samples/).
- **Specification stability:** Device API is a Candidate Recommendation Draft; several extensions remain Working or Editor's Drafts. Pin the exact tested spec revision(s), distinguish normative requirements from proposals, and do not silently infer real hardware support from a virtual profile name.

## Pre-merge acceptance

### Specification inventory and core conformance
- [ ] Produce a versioned feature/API inventory (e.g. `docs/webxr-conformance.md`) mapping **each of the two device profiles and their VR/MR/AR modes** to implemented / unsupported WebXR core and relevant modules, matching advertised `requiredFeatures`/`optionalFeatures`. Link specification sections and reproducible tests for claims of support.
- [ ] Bring **WebXR Device API core** behavior in line with the selected current W3C draft: session mode support and request lifecycle, required/optional feature negotiation and introspection (`enabledFeatures`), appropriate DOMException names and promise-vs-synchronous errors, session end, visibility/events, correct XRFrame lifetime and state checks, requestAnimationFrame ordering, frame/predicted display behavior where observable, input source lifecycle/event ordering, and profile/mode-dependent capabilities.
- [ ] Correct **reference spaces and spatial math** (`viewer`, `local`, `local-floor`, and optional `bounded-floor`/`unbounded` only if implemented), transformations, offset reference spaces, `XRRigidTransform`, `XRPose`, XRView eye and projection semantics, seated/standing behavior, invalid or unavailable poses, world-to-reference coordinate conversions, and renderer/framebuffer/viewport semantics. Preserve correct Quest stereoscopic VR/MR, phone monoscopic AR, high-DPI and resize behavior.
- [ ] Match the **WebXR AR Module** semantics for immersive-ar composition and visibility, with deterministic virtual-room data where a real-world environment is unavailable; do not imply real camera passthrough/occlusion or sensor fidelity.

### Existing extension APIs that must be fixed
- [ ] Implement the published **Hit Test** API's supported ray, plane/point/mesh entity filtering as applicable, `offsetRay`, session feature checks, active frame/source ownership checks, ended/inactive/cancelled source semantics, specified errors, transient input source/profile association, results ordering, and returned surface-normal orientation. Add negative/edge-case tests, not just a successful room intersection.
- [ ] Correct **DOM Overlay** required/optional feature negotiation, missing/invalid `domOverlay.root`, `domOverlayState`, visibility, beforexrselect/input interaction, and cleanup on end; only advertise actual interaction capabilities.
- [ ] Verify and repair **Gamepads / controller input** (Quest controller profiles, mapping, handedness, axes/buttons incl. select/squeeze event order and source changes) and **handheld touch** (`screen`/transient input). Tests must exercise frame-by-frame state transitions, not only button presence.

### Modern extension module implementation targets
- [ ] Implement a deterministic **WebXR Anchors** simulation for AR/MR: create/delete anchors relative to real `XRSpace` results, report poses across frames, keep stable anchors when the simulated viewer moves, clean up at session end, and expose the appropriate feature descriptor and interface(s).
- [ ] Implement a deterministic **WebXR Hand Input** simulation for Quest 3 (not an Android phone capability): correctly shaped hand/joint collection, joint spaces, joint poses/radii, source hand presence/absence, and a controllable or reproducible input state. Do not claim real optical tracking.
- [ ] Add usable **WebXR Layers** support appropriate for a desktop emulator (modern `XRWebGLBinding`, projection layer and at least a simple composition layer path, coherent subimages/viewports, lifecycle and texture/frame semantics). Preserve working `XRWebGLLayer` legacy clients.
- [ ] Add a consistent simulated **Depth Sensing** path for eligible AR/MR sessions using the virtual room's geometry, with correct feature negotiation, depth formats/units, and CPU/GPU exposure only for actually supported modes and formats; return consistent depth/pose values and required errors. Do not manufacture a claim of actual hardware depth.
- [ ] Add a deterministic **Lighting Estimation** implementation for AR/MR using the virtual scene's lighting, with lifecycle/feature negotiation and probe data following the chosen published/draft API; explicitly distinguish virtual estimates from real environmental sensor measurements.

### Build, tests and documentation
- [ ] Modernize/replace/update the upstream polyfill internals only as necessary, keep maintained code strict TypeScript, avoid unrelated framework/manifest/device-profile changes, and ensure MV3 MAIN-world synchronous `navigator.xr` initialization, CSP-safe packaged injection, isolated privileged bridge, worker restart recovery, multi-frame routing, and Firefox MV3 packaging remain correct.
- [ ] Extend automated **spec-based tests** (Web Platform Tests where feasible, plus focused equivalent tests for the emulator) to cover public API shape, feature negotiation and errors, lifecycle, frame validity, transforms, session transitions, Hit Test/DOM Overlay, and the new extension paths on each profile. Document executed WPT cases, any required harness adaptations, passed/failed/skipped cases, and reasons. Do not claim entire WPT suite conformance without running it.
- [ ] Run and record `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run build`, `npm run build:firefox`, `npm run test:browser`, and applicable new conformance tests on a current desktop Chrome/Chromium build. Verify Quest VR/MR and Android AR in the real unpacked extension/DevTools panel, use representative WebXR sample apps when executable, and document any Firefox runtime limitations. Include both successful and deliberate feature-rejection scenarios.
- [ ] Update README and versioned conformance documentation with actual supported APIs, profile-specific capabilities, clear extension/draft limitations, emulator-vs-real-hardware differences, and reproducible test instructions. Remove outdated 2019-spec claims once they are no longer true; do not describe unimplemented features as supported.
- [ ] Create implementation PR(s) against `dev`, follow the repository template and review process, and close this Issue **only when all mandatory scope above is implemented and validated**. If work is split into smaller PRs, keep this Issue open until the full listed acceptance criteria are met; disclose any incomplete areas rather than checking them off.

## Optional validation

- Execute Firefox MV3 runtime/DevTools tests on a supported Firefox release if available.
- Run real-device comparisons on Quest 3 or Android ARCore where hardware is available; physical devices are **not** a mandatory pre-merge condition for an emulator.
- Test additional browser versions, third-party Three.js/Babylon.js/A-Frame WebXR samples and performance regressions beyond the focused acceptance suite.

## Required post-merge verification

None. Applicable conformance, build, browser, and documentation checks must be verified before merge. Store publication and hardware certification are outside this Issue.
